title: The tests are the assignment
blurb: Three minutes at the terminal. It shows the tool that grades you, and never opens the file you are writing.

cues.text: Module 1 asks you for three small functions in one file.
This video never opens that file. Your answer stays yours.
What it shows you is the tool that decides whether the three are right.
You can run that tool as often as you like before the deadline.
The three sit under one banner, extension point 3 of 5.
should retry asks one question. Is this request worth sending again?
backoff seconds says how long to wait before you try.
parse json content reads a reply, or says clearly why it could not.
None of the three needs a network or a key. They are pure logic.
So the whole assignment runs offline, on your own machine.
Run the tests before you write anything, so you know what failing looks like.
The output goes through tail, so you see the summary and no assertion detail.
Eleven failed, six passed. Say that count out loud.
That is a starting line, not a problem.
Then open the test file itself and read it.
Every failing name points at a rule the docstring already gave you.
It is the clearest statement of what your three functions have to do.
Reading it is part of the job, not a way around the job.
Here is the same command against finished work, with the whole output this time.
Seventeen passed, in well under a second.
No request went anywhere. That is what pure logic looks like.
There is no key to burn here and no rate limit to wait on.
So run it after every small change you make.
Now save your proof. Send the same output into a file.
Nothing printed, because the output went into the file instead.
So open the file and read it back. Seventeen passed, and the file is not empty.
An empty proof file is a submission with no proof in it.
Check that before you upload, not after.
One warning before you start.
Say you write should retry so it says yes to every client error, and nothing crashes.
Then a 401 arrives. Your key is not accepted, and your loop keeps trying.
Your provider's daily limit is gone in about four seconds, on a request that could never succeed.
Then you are locked out until tomorrow, and the work is due tonight.
That is why the rule is narrow. Retry only what waiting can fix.
Upload two files. Your edited model client, and your saved pytest output.
Not the whole repository, and never the file that holds your key.
If you get stuck, paste the test name and the message on the Q and A board.
Paste the failure, not your answer.
Being stuck costs nobody points. Being quiet about it costs time.
